mainTopic: Rules of public reading: voices and translators, the מגילה ברכות, the number of readers and פסוקים, ברכות for each עולה, and dividing the ראש חודש reading.
overview: The גמרא begins with how many people may read and translate at the same time. The rule is strictest for the תורה, looser for נביא, and very loose for הלל and מגילה, because people love the מגילה and listen closely. אביי then rules that the ברכה before the מגילה is always required, based on שמואל's rule of עובר לעשייתן, and three פסוקים prove that עובר means 'before'. The גמרא gives the three ברכות said before the מגילה (מנ״ח) and the ברכה said after it, where רב פפא combines two endings. Next it explains the three readers on Monday, Thursday and שבת at מנחה, and the minimum of ten פסוקים, with several ideas about what each number stands for. רבא teaches that any of the three readers may read four פסוקים, and each position has its own reason for praise. The גמרא explains why today every עולה says both ברכות. Finally עולא בר רב asks how four readers can split the ראש חודש reading, and the options being tested continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Two readers are not allowed for קריאת התורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds to the משנה: two people may read the מגילה together, but this is not the case for קריאת התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: which is not the case for the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה said that one person or two people may read the מגילה. The ברייתא adds that this is not allowed for reading the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the מגילה, two people may read aloud at the same time. With the תורה, only one voice may read at a time. This sets up the fuller ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.english: It was taught: which is not so with the Torah.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's words 'one reads or two read' for the מגילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that limits the scope of the משנה's rule about two readers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people reading at once is allowed for the מגילה but not for the תורה.

steps.title: How many readers and translators for תורה, נביא, הלל and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a sliding scale. For תורה: one reader and one translator. For נביא: one reader and up to two translators. For הלל and מגילה: even ten and ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In the תורה, one reads and one translates, as long as there are not one reading and two translating. In the נביא, one reads and two translate, as long as there are not two reading and two translating. In הלל and מגילה, even ten may read and ten may translate.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא lists how many voices may be heard at once during public reading and its translation into Aramaic, for each type of reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תורה, every word must be heard clearly because it teaches הלכה, so only one voice may speak at a time. Only one person may read the נביא in Hebrew, but two may translate together, because exact comprehension of the translation is less critical than for the תורה. For הלל and מגילה there is almost no limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Translator who says the reading aloud in Aramaic
Hallel, the praise of ה׳ said on festivals

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'two' means two voices speaking at the same time, not two people taking turns.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: in the Torah,
one reads and one translates,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אֶחָד קוֹרֵא וּשְׁנַיִם מְתַרְגְּמִין.
phrases.english: as long as there is not one reading and two translating.
phrases.notes: Two translators speaking together cannot both be heard clearly.

phrases.english: And in the Prophets, one reads and two translate,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ שְׁנַיִם קוֹרִין וּשְׁנַיִם מְתַרְגְּמִין.
phrases.english: as long as there are not two reading and two translating.
And in Hallel and the Megillah,
even ten may read and ten may translate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out in full the difference that step 1 only hinted at.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה: one voice at a time. נביא: one reader; up to two simultaneous translators. הלל and מגילה: even ten voices.

steps.title: Why may many people read the מגילה together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that הלל and מגילה allow so many voices at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. If two voices are normally hard to hear, why are ten allowed for the מגילה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual problem is that the listener cannot follow several voices at once. The question is what makes the מגילה different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind the last clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why הלל and מגילה do not have the problem that several voices cannot be heard together.

steps.title: Because it is beloved, people listen closely
steps.stepSummary: Because the מגילה (and הלל) is dear to people, they pay close attention and hear it, even with many voices.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is beloved, they pay attention and hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that love for the מגילה makes people focus, so several voices do not stop them from hearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against several voices exists to make sure people actually hear. When the listeners care a lot, they hear anyway, so the limit is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They give their attention, they focus

steps.whatToRemember: The limit on voices depends on whether people can really hear. Love for the מגילה makes people listen closely.

phrases.english: Since it is beloved,
they pay attention and hear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the מגילה is beloved, people focus and hear it even with many voices.

steps.title: משנה: where the custom is to bless, one blesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Whether to say a ברכה on the מגילה depends on local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: A place where they are accustomed to recite a blessing, one should recite a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This is a setup line for אביי's comment that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה suggests that the ברכה on the מגילה is only a custom. That idea is about to be limited.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where the custom is

phrases.english: A place where they are accustomed to bless, one should bless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on the מגילה follows local custom.

steps.title: אביי: the custom applies only to the blessing after
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה's 'follow the custom' applies only to the ברכה after the reading. The ברכה before is always a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this about the blessing after it, but before it, it is a מצוה to bless.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the משנה. Only the ברכה after the reading depends on custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made the whole ברכה sound optional. אביי splits it in two: the ברכה before is required everywhere, and only the ברכה after depends on custom.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to bless

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing with the משנה. He is explaining that it only means the ברכה after the reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, the ברכות before reading the מגילה are said everywhere.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאַחֲרֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Abaye said: they only taught this regarding after it,
but before it, it is a מצוה to bless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאַחֲרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה before the מגילה is required. Only the ברכה after depends on custom.

steps.title: שמואל: every מצוה gets its blessing beforehand
steps.stepSummary: Support for אביי from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: for all מצוות, one says the ברכה עובר לעשייתן, before doing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: For all the מצוות, one blesses over them before doing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where אביי's rule comes from: a general rule that a ברכה is said before doing any מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every מצוה needs a ברכה before it, the ברכה before the מגילה cannot be optional. The ברכה after is not covered by this rule, so it can depend on custom.

keyTerms.meaning: All the מצוות, every one of them

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of עובר לעשייתן: a ברכה on a מצוה is said before the מצוה is done.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule for ברכות on all מצוות.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
for all the מצוות, one blesses over them
before ("over") their performance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind אביי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברכה before the מגילה is required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's general rule: every מצוה gets its ברכה עובר לעשייתן.

steps.title: How do we know עובר means 'before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the word עובר means 'before'. It could also mean 'passing' or 'after'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is it implied that this word 'over' is a term for coming first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the meaning of the word עובר in שמואל's rule. This sets up the proofs from פסוקים that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עובר usually means 'passing by'. The גמרא wants to show from the Torah's language that it can mean 'going ahead of'.

keyTerms.meaning: A term for coming first, going ahead

phrases.english: From where is it implied that this word "over"
is a term for going first?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי עוֹבֵר לִישָּׁנָא דְּאַקְדּוֹמֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the key word in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that עובר means 'ahead of'.

steps.title: Proof from אחימעץ overtaking the כושי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the פסוק where אחימעץ ran and 'ויעבר' the Cushite, meaning he got ahead of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The פסוק says, 'And אחימעץ ran by the way of the plain and overtook the כושי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves from a פסוק that עבר can mean getting ahead of someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, אחימעץ raced the Cushite runner and arrived first. ויעבר there must mean 'passed and went ahead of', so עובר means 'before'.

keyTerms.meaning: אחימעץ, a runner in the time of דוד

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
the verse says: "And Achimaatz ran by way of the plain,
and overtook the Cushite."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויעבר את הכושי means he got ahead of the Cushite, so עבר means 'going first'.

steps.title: אביי's proof: יעקב went before them
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a different פסוק: יעקב 'עבר לפניהם', went ahead of his family.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, from here: 'And he passed before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second source. Here יעקב walked in front of his family as they went to meet עשו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק says 'לפניהם', before them, right next to עבר, which makes the meaning 'going ahead' very clear. It may be clearer than רב נחמן's proof, where 'ahead' has to be inferred from the story.

phrases.english: Abaye said: from here:
"And he passed before them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the same question, instead of רב נחמן's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והוא עבר לפניהם' shows that עבר means going ahead.

steps.title: Another proof: their king passed before them
steps.stepSummary: A third option: the פסוק in מיכה, 'ויעבר מלכם לפניהם וה׳ בראשם', where their king goes ahead of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it is from here: 'And their king passed before them, and the Lord at their head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers one more פסוק as an extra choice for proving that עבר means 'before'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here עבר is paired with 'לפניהם' and with 'בראשם', at their head. That strongly shows the idea of leading in front.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say instead

steps.whatToRemember: Three פסוקים prove that עובר means 'before', which supports the rule of עובר לעשייתן. So the ברכה before the מגילה is always required.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: from here:
"And their king passed before them,
and the Lord at their head."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third alternative source for the same point.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויעבר מלכם לפניהם' shows that עבר means leading in front.

steps.title: Which blessing is said before the מגילה reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ברכה is said before reading the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the reading of the מגילה, what ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: Having just proven that ברכות are said before a מצוה, the גמרא now asks which ברכות are actually said before reading the מגילה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7–11 established the general rule that a ברכה comes עובר לעשייתן, before the action. Now the גמרא moves from 'when' to 'what': it wants the actual wording of the ברכות said before the מגילה.

phrases.english: Before it, what blessing does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general timing rule (before the מצוה) to the specific text of the ברכות before the מגילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of the ברכות recited before קריאת המגילה.

steps.title: רב ששת recited three blessings, hinted at by the letters מנ״ח
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב ששת from קטרזיא came before רב אשי and recited the ברכות hinted at by מנ״ח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת from קטרזיא happened to come before רב אשי, and he recited the ברכות of מנ״ח: על מקרא מגילה, שעשה נסים, and שהחיינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story. A scholar read the מגילה in front of רב אשי and said three ברכות, which are hinted at by the letters מ, נ, and ח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from what was actually done in front of a great authority, רב אשי. מנ״ח is a memory device: מ stands for מקרא (reading the מגילה), נ for נסים (the miracles), and ח for שהחיינו (Who has kept us alive).

keyTerms.meaning: Acronym for the three ברכות before the מגילה

steps.confusionAlert: מנ״ח here is NOT the word מנחה (the afternoon prayer). It is an abbreviation for three ברכות: מקרא, נסים, שהחיינו.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet from Katrazya
phrases.notes: Not the famous blind רב ששת; this is a different scholar from a place called קטרזיא.

phrases.english: happened to come before Rav Ashi
and he recited M-N-Ch (Mikra, Nissim, Shehecheyanu).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִקַּטְרַזְיָא אִיקְּלַע לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with an actual case done before רב אשי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three ברכות are said before the מגילה: על מקרא מגילה, שעשה נסים, and שהחיינו.

steps.title: Which blessing is said after the מגילה reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what ברכה is said after reading the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the reading of the מגילה, what ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the closing ברכה said after the מגילה. This sets up the text of the ברכה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה noted that some places have a custom to say a ברכה after the reading. The גמרא now wants the wording of that ברכה.

phrases.english: After it, what blessing does one recite?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to step 12, now about the ברכה after the reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברכה recited after קריאת המגילה.

steps.title: The blessing of הרב את ריבנו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the full text of the ברכה after the מגילה, ending 'הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the world, (the God) Who fights our fight, judges our case, takes our revenge, punishes our enemies for us, and pays back everyone who hates us. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who punishes all of Israel's enemies on their behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the whole closing ברכה, the one still said today after the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה praises ה׳ for standing up for the Jewish people against their enemies, as happened in the פורים story with המן. Its ending (the חתימה) here is 'הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם'. The next steps discuss this ending.

keyTerms.meaning: Who fights our fight / pleads our cause

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe
(the God) Who fights our fight
and Who judges our case
and Who takes our revenge
and Who punishes our enemies for us
and Who pays back all the enemies of our soul,

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הַנִּפְרָע לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִכׇּל צָרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who punishes all their enemies on behalf of Israel.
phrases.notes: This is the חתימה (closing line) according to this first version.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם (הָאֵל) הָרָב אֶת רִיבֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 with the full text of the ברכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה הרב את ריבנו, ending 'הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם'.

steps.title: רבא's different ending: the God Who saves
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברכה ends with 'האל המושיע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the ending is 'the God Who saves'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different closing line for the same ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is only about the חתימה, the final 'ברוך אתה ה׳' line. The first version focuses on punishing the enemies. רבא's version focuses on ה׳ saving us.

phrases.english: Rava said: 'The God Who saves.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different ending for the ברכה quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חתימה of the ברכה after the מגילה is 'האל המושיע'.

steps.title: רב פפא: say both endings together
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that, because of the disagreement, we combine both endings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, let us say both of them: 'Blessed are You, ה׳, Who punishes all their enemies on behalf of Israel, the God Who saves.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since there are two versions of the ending, רב פפא rules that we say both together. That is our practice today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing one opinion, רב פפא combines them so that both are satisfied. The word הלכך ('therefore') shows that this follows directly from the existence of two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Before the מגילה: three ברכות (מנ״ח). After it: הרב את ריבנו, ending with both phrases, 'הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם האל המושיע'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact ending found in our סידורים today after the מגילה reading.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore —
let us say both of them:

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הַנִּפְרָע לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִכׇּל צָרֵיהֶם
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who punishes all their enemies on behalf of Israel,
the God Who saves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ נֵימְרִינְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the disagreement between step 15 and step 16 by combining them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה after the מגילה ends: 'ברוך אתה ה׳ הנפרע לישראל מכל צריהם האל המושיע'.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: three people read on Monday, Thursday, and שבת at מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on Monday, Thursday, and שבת at מנחה, three people read from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday and Thursday, and on שבת at מנחה, three people read from the תורה, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is the base text for the next discussion. The question will be why the number is specifically three.

keyTerms.meaning: On Monday and Thursday (the second and fifth days)
On שבת at the afternoon service

steps.confusionAlert: Read this as three separate times: Monday, Thursday, and שבת at מנחה. It does NOT mean that on Monday and Thursday the reading is at מנחה. On Monday and Thursday the reading is in the morning.

phrases.english: On Monday and on Thursday, and on Shabbat at the afternoon service,
three people read, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי בַּשַּׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה קוֹרִין שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: leaves the מגילה ברכות and returns to the משנה about קריאת התורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three people are called to the תורה on Monday, Thursday, and שבת at מנחה.

steps.title: What do the three readers correspond to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the number three represents.
steps.simpleTranslation: These three, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source or symbolism behind the number three. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Numbers in rabbinic rules often stand for something. The גמרא wants to know what the three readers are meant to represent.

phrases.english: These three, corresponding to what are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the number in the משנה quoted in step 18.

steps.title: רב אסי: תורה, נביאים, and כתובים
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי says the three readers correspond to the three parts of תנ״ך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: they correspond to תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives the first answer: the three readers match the three sections of the Jewish Bible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer links the number to the three parts of written Scripture.

keyTerms.meaning: The Five Books, the Prophets, and the Writings (תנ״ך)

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
Corresponding to Torah, Prophets, and Writings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: כְּנֶגֶד תּוֹרָה נְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three readers correspond to תורה, נביאים, and כתובים.

steps.title: רבא: כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the three readers correspond to the three groups of the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: they correspond to כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer: the three readers match the three groups within the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא links the number to people rather than books. This fits the familiar order of the עליות: first a כהן, then a לוי, then a ישראל.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Corresponding to Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three readers correspond to כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים.

steps.title: What do רב שימי's ten verses correspond to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב שימי's rule that a reading has at least ten פסוקים, and asks what the ten correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב שימי taught: one may not read fewer than ten פסוקים in the בית הכנסת, and a פסוק like 'וידבר' counts toward the number. These ten, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of 'what does the number stand for', the גמרא brings another number, ten פסוקים, and asks what it represents. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining the three readers, the גמרא applies the same question to the minimum of ten פסוקים in a public reading. רב שימי also adds that even a plain introductory פסוק like 'וידבר ה׳ אל משה לאמר' counts toward the ten.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not go below / reduce
'And He spoke', a standard introductory פסוק

phrases.english: But that which Rav Shimi taught:
One may not read fewer than ten verses
in the synagogue,
and 'And He spoke' counts toward the number.
These ten, corresponding to what are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'כנגד מי' question from the three readers to the ten פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the minimum of ten פסוקים in a public reading symbolizes.

steps.title: The ten verses match the ten men who sit in shul
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the ten פסוקים correspond to the ten בטלנין in the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The ten verses correspond to the ten men who are free and always sit in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from step 22: what do the ten פסוקים correspond to? רבי יהושע בן לוי links them to the ten בטלנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בטלנין here is not an insult. It means ten men who are free from work and always present in shul, so there is always a מנין for communal needs. Ten פסוקים match these ten people who make up a community.

keyTerms.meaning: Men free from work who are always in the בית הכנסת to serve the community

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read בטלנין as 'lazy people.' Here it means dedicated men who are free to always be in shul.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
They correspond to the ten idle men who are in the synagogue.
phrases.notes: Men who are free from work and available for communal needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כְּנֶגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ten פסוקים correspond to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten בטלנין of the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: The ten verses match the עשרת הדברות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ten פסוקים correspond to the עשרת הדברות said to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They correspond to the עשרת הדברות that were said to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. רב יוסף connects the ten פסוקים to the עשרת הדברות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading Torah reenacts receiving the Torah at סיני. So it makes sense that the minimum reading mirrors the ten statements given there.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the Torah was given

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
They correspond to the Ten Commandments
that were said to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף: אָמַר כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ten פסוקים correspond to.

steps.title: The ten verses match דוד's ten praises in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says the ten פסוקים correspond to the ten expressions of praise that דוד said in ספר תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: They correspond to the ten praises that דוד said in ספר תהלים.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer, printed in parentheses in our text. רבי לוי ties the ten פסוקים to ten praises in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parentheses show this line was not in every manuscript. It still follows the same pattern: a well-known set of ten in תנ״ך explains the number ten.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
They correspond to the ten praises
that David said in the book of Psalms.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה הִילּוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ten פסוקים correspond to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten praises of דוד in תהלים.

steps.title: The ten verses match the ten statements of creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ten פסוקים correspond to the עשרה מאמרות with which the world was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: They correspond to the ten statements with which the world was created.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer. רבי יוחנן links the ten פסוקים to the ten divine statements of creation. The גמרא will now examine this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view connects Torah reading to the creation of the world. It also invites a counting question, because the reader will want to know which ten statements are meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The ten divine statements with which the world was created

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
They correspond to the ten statements
with which the world was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the alternative answers to step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ten פסוקים correspond to.

steps.title: Which are the ten statements of creation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the ten מאמרות are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a check of רבי יוחנן's view by asking which ten statements he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a clarifying question, not an attack. It asks for the list, so that the count can be tested in the next steps.

phrases.english: Which are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the ten מאמרות.

steps.title: The statements are the 'And He said' lines in בראשית
steps.stepSummary: The ten מאמרות are the times the creation story says ויאמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'And God said' statements of בראשית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the statements are the lines that begin with ויאמר אלקים in the first chapter of בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the obvious way to identify them. Each ויאמר introduces a new act of creation, so each one counts as a מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: And He said (the creation formula 'And God said')
The book of Genesis / the creation story

phrases.english: The 'And He said' of Genesis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ויאמר statements in the creation story.

steps.title: But there are only nine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that there are only nine ויאמר statements, not ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are only nine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the identification it just gave. If you count the ויאמר lines in creation, you get nine, not ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count does not match רבי יוחנן's claim of ten. Either the identification or the number must be fixed.

phrases.english: These are nine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there are ten מאמרות of creation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the ויאמר statements gives only nine.

steps.title: בראשית itself counts as a statement
steps.stepSummary: The word בראשית also counts as a מאמר, as the פסוק in תהלים says the heavens were made by הקב״ה's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the beginning' is also a statement, as it is written: 'By the word of ה׳ the heavens were made, and all their hosts by the breath of His mouth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The first פסוק, בראשית ברא, is also a מאמר, which makes ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the first פסוק does not say ויאמר, the פסוק in תהלים teaches that the heavens were made through הקב״ה's word. So the original creation of heaven and earth was also done by speech and counts as the tenth מאמר.
steps.whatToRemember: The ten מאמרות are the nine ויאמר lines plus בראשית, which counts as a statement based on the פסוק 'בדבר ה׳ שמים נעשו'.

phrases.english: 'In the beginning' is also a statement,
as it is written:
'By the word of the Lord the heavens were made,'
'and all their host by the breath of His mouth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expands the count to include an unstated item, supported by a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only lines that say ויאמר count, giving nine.
steps.terutzMaskana: בראשית is also a מאמר, making ten.

steps.title: Any reader who reads four verses is praiseworthy
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that whether the first, second, or third reader reads four of the ten פסוקים, he is praiseworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The first who read four is praiseworthy; the second who read four is praiseworthy; the third who read four is praiseworthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new practical teaching. Three readers share ten פסוקים, so one of them must read four, and רבא says that is praiseworthy for any of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten does not split evenly among three, so the split is 4-3-3. רבא says each option has a reason to be praised, and the גמרא will now explain each reason, starting with the first reader.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical guidance for dividing the minimum reading among three עולים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The first who read four is praiseworthy;
the second who read four is praiseworthy;
the third who read four is praiseworthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁקָּרָא אַרְבָּעָה — מְשׁוּבָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב שימי's ten-פסוק rule with a new practical teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whichever of the three readers reads four פסוקים is praiseworthy.

steps.title: Why the first reader deserves praise: the three numbered baskets
steps.stepSummary: The first reader is praised because, as the משנה about תרומת הלשכה shows, the מצוה is greater with what comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first who read four is praiseworthy, as we learned: With three baskets of three se'ah each, they would take money out of the chamber. Written on them was alef, beis, gimmel, to know which was taken out first, so they could bring offerings from it first, because the מצוה is with the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins proving each part of רבא's rule, starting with the first reader. It brings a משנה about the Temple funds to show that being first carries extra importance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית המקדש, money was taken out in three baskets labeled א, ב, ג, and the first basket's money was used first, because there is a special מצוה in what is first. In the same way, the first reader, who reads the larger share of four, is praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking money out of the Temple treasury chamber for communal offerings
Because the מצוה is with the first

phrases.english: The first who read four is praiseworthy,
as we learned in a mishnah:
With three baskets of three se'ah each
with which they take the funds out of the chamber,
phrases.notes: The chamber here is the Temple treasury, the one talked about in מסכת שקלים.

phrases.english: and on them was written alef, beis, gimmel,
to know which of them was taken out first,
in order to bring offerings from it first,
because the מצוה is with the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first clause of רבא's rule from step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That the first reader who reads four is praiseworthy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שקלים about three labeled baskets, showing that the מצוה is greater with the first.

steps.title: The middle reader is praiseworthy, learned from the מנורה's middle lamp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about the מנורה shows that the middle position is honored, so the middle reader who reads four is praiseworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the middle reader read four פסוקים, he is praiseworthy. As a ברייתא teaches: 'Toward the face of the מנורה the lamps shall give light.' This teaches that the כהן turns the lamps toward the western lamp, and the western lamp faces the שכינה. And רבי יוחנן said: from here we learn that the middle one is praiseworthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now proves the second part of רבא's teaching: why the middle reader is also praised if he reads the extra פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מנורה, the outer lamps all turn toward the middle lamp (the נר מערבי), and that lamp faces the שכינה. So the middle spot is the place of honor. רבי יוחנן learns from this that the middle reader holds an honored position too.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle one (here, the second of three readers)
The western lamp, the middle lamp of the מנורה

steps.confusionAlert: The 'western lamp' here is the middle lamp of the מנורה. That is why it proves the middle reader is honored.

phrases.english: The middle one who read four is praiseworthy
as it is taught in a baraita:
"Toward the face of the menorah they shall give light"
this teaches that he turns their fronts
toward the western lamp
and the western lamp faces toward the Divine Presence.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
from here we learn that the middle one is praiseworthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 32: step 32 proved the first reader, this step proves the middle reader.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the middle reader who reads four is praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on 'אל מול פני המנורה יאירו' plus רבי יוחנן's derivation

steps.title: The last reader is praiseworthy because we go up in holiness
steps.stepSummary: The last reader who reads four is praised because of the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the last reader read four, he is praiseworthy, because we go up in holiness and do not go down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the third part of רבא's teaching: why the last reader is praised for reading four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the last reader reads the most פסוקים, the reading grows as it goes on. That fits the rule that in holy matters we increase and do not decrease. So each of the three positions has its own reason for being praised.

keyTerms.meaning: We go up in holiness and do not go down

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, any of the three readers may take the fourth פסוק. First: the מצוה is greater with what comes first. Middle: like the middle lamp of the מנורה. Last: מעלין בקודש.

phrases.english: And the last one who read four is praiseworthy
because one elevates in holiness and does not lower.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part justification that began in step 32.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the last reader who reads four is praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general principle מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין

steps.title: רב פפא praises a first reader who read four
steps.stepSummary: A story: in the shul of אבי גובר the first reader read four פסוקים, and רב פפא praised him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא happened to come to the shul of אבי גובר. The first reader read four פסוקים, and רב פפא praised him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows רבא's rule in real life: a great אמורא praised a first reader who took the extra פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's praise confirms in practice that reading four as the first reader is good, as step 32 explained. The story backs up the ruling with real behavior.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa happened to come
to the synagogue of Avi Gover
and the first one read four,
and Rav Pappa praised him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Real-life support for the first case of רבא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a first reader who reads four is praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב פפא's praise in the shul of אבי גובר

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's limit on readers and a ברייתא on who makes the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה's words 'we neither decrease nor add' and brings a ברייתא: the first reader blesses before and the last reader blesses after.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: we do not have fewer readers or add more. A ברייתא teaches: the one who opens the reading says a ברכה before it, and the one who closes says a ברכה after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains the original way the ברכות were said. This sets up the next step, which deals with today's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally, only two ברכות were said for the whole reading: one by the first reader at the start, and one by the last reader at the end. The middle readers said no ברכה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not decrease and do not add
The one who opens (the first reader)
The one who closes (the last reader)

phrases.english: We do not decrease from them and we do not add.
It was taught in a baraita:
The one who opens recites a blessing before it,
and the one who closes recites a blessing after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the division of פסוקים to the next phrase of the משנה and the topic of ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, only the first reader says a ברכה before the reading, and only the last reader says a ברכה after it.

steps.title: Why every reader says both blessings today
steps.stepSummary: Today every reader blesses before and after. The רבנן made this rule because of people who come in late or leave early.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when all the readers say ברכות before and after, this is the reason the רבנן made this rule: it is a decree because of those who come in and because of those who go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why today's practice is different from the ברייתא: now every reader says both ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who walks in late would miss the first ברכה. Someone who leaves early would miss the last ברכה. Either one might think the reading needs only one ברכה. So the רבנן had every reader say both, so that anyone present hears a full set.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who come in and those who go out

steps.whatToRemember: The original rule was one ברכה at the start and one at the end. Today every עולה says both, as a גזירה for people who come late or leave early.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's rule was not rejected as wrong. The רבנן added to it later as a protective measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for our practice today, where every עולה says a ברכה before and after his עליה.

phrases.english: And nowadays,
that all of them recite blessings before it and after it,
this is the reason that the Sages instituted it:
a decree because of those who enter
and because of those who leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unstated question of why today's practice differs from the ברייתא in step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Later rabbinic enactment (גזירה) explains the change in practice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Today's practice seems to contradict the ברייתא, which has only two ברכות in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן later enacted that every reader blesses before and after, so latecomers and early leavers are not misled.

steps.title: The משנה: four people read on ראש חודש and חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on ראש חודש and חול המועד, four people are called to the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: On ראש חודש and on חול המועד, four people read, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the next discussion: how exactly do four people split the ראש חודש reading?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya discussed how many פסוקים each reader reads and who makes the ברכות. Now the focus moves to the special days of ראש חודש and חול המועד, where the number of readers is set at four. The word וכו׳ means the גמרא is quoting only the start of the line.

keyTerms.meaning: New Moons. The first day(s) of each Jewish month.
The intermediate days of a Yom Tov (חול המועד)
"Etc.". The quote from the משנה continues.

phrases.english: On New Moons and on the intermediate days of a Festival
four people read, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים וּבְחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד קוֹרִין אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of ברכות before and after the reading to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש and חול המועד, four people are called to the Torah.

steps.title: עולא בר רב asks how to split the ראש חודש reading
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר רב asks רבא how four people can read the ראש חודש portion. Its first section, צו את בני ישראל, has eight פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר רב asked רבא: The ראש חודש portion, how do we read it? The section "Command the children of Israel and say to them, My offering, My bread" has eight פסוקים. What should we do?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks a practical question. How do we divide the ראש חודש Torah reading among four people?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading has three short sections: 8 פסוקים (the daily offering), 2 (שבת), and 5 (ראש חודש). Each of the four readers needs at least three פסוקים. The rules about where you may stop and start make this hard to split. The question starts with the first section of eight פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him. This introduces a question put to a teacher.
The Torah portion read on ראש חודש (במדבר כ״ח:א׳-ט״ו)
What should we do? / How should we act?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the whole reading as one block of 15 פסוקים. The difficulty comes from the fact that it is made of three separate פרשיות (8 + 2 + 5). The rules about stopping and starting apply to each פרשה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ עוּלָּא בַּר רַב מֵרָבָא:
phrases.english: Ulla bar Rav asked of Rava:
The portion of the New Moon,
how do we read it?
"Command the children of Israel
and say to them: My offering, My bread",
which is eight verses,
what should we do?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ עוּלָּא בַּר רַב מֵרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the משנה's rule of four readers
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to divide the 15-פסוק ראש חודש portion (8 + 2 + 5) among four readers

steps.title: Three verses each for the first two readers does not work
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the first two readers each read three פסוקים. Then only two פסוקים are left in the first פרשה, and you may not stop with fewer than three left in a פרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose two readers read three פסוקים each. Then two are left. But we do not leave fewer than three פסוקים in a פרשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a first way to split the reading and rejects it because it breaks a rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 3 + 3 = 6, which leaves 2 פסוקים at the end of the 8-פסוק section. There is a rule that a reader may not stop when fewer than three פסוקים remain in the פרשה. So the second reader would be stopping in a forbidden place.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him read. This introduces a suggested option.
We do not leave over in a פרשה (fewer than three פסוקים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of two placement rules that control the whole sugya. Every option that follows is checked against it.

phrases.english: Let two read
three verses each —
two remain,
and we do not leave over in a paragraph
fewer than three verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first possible answer to the question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option of 3 + 3 פסוקים for the first two readers
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves only 2 פסוקים in the פרשה, which breaks the rule of אין משיירין פחות משלשה

steps.title: Four verses each causes a problem with the remaining seven
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the first two readers each read four פסוקים and finish the first פרשה. Then seven פסוקים are left: two in וביום השבת and five in ובראשי חדשיכם. How do the last two readers split them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose they read four each. Then seven are left. "And on the day of שבת" is two פסוקים, and "And on your New Moons" is five. What should we do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second split. This fixes the first section, but it creates a new problem with the remaining sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 4 + 4 finishes the 8-פסוק section cleanly. But the two remaining readers now face a 2-פסוק section followed by a 5-פסוק section. The 2-פסוק section is too short to be one person's whole reading, and it is awkward to divide anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: "And on the day of שבת". This is the 2-פסוק section about the שבת offering.
"And on your New Moons". This is the 5-פסוק section about the ראש חודש offering.

phrases.english: Let them read four each —
seven remain,
"And on the day of Shabbat" is two,
"And on your New Moons" is five,
what should we do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 3 + 3 option fails, a 4 + 4 option is tried and runs into a new difficulty
steps.kashyaTarget: The option of 4 + 4 פסוקים for the first two readers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The remaining 2 + 5 פסוקים cannot easily be split between two readers who each need three

steps.title: Testing two verses from the שבת section plus one from the next
steps.stepSummary: A further option: the third reader reads the two פסוקים of the שבת section plus one פסוק from the ראש חודש section. The problem with this is stated on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him read two from this one and one from those —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes another way to split the remaining seven פסוקים. This line sets up a rejection that comes right after, on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 2 + 1 gives the third reader his three פסוקים, and the last reader would read the remaining 4. But the third reader would start the ראש חודש section and read only one of its פסוקים. As the next passage shows, the problem is that you may not begin a פרשה by reading fewer than three of its פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is a suggestion that is being tested, not the גמרא's answer. Its rejection comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Let him read two from this one
and one from those —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a way to handle the remaining seven פסוקים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the third reader may combine 2 פסוקים from the שבת section with 1 from the ראש חודש section
